Soak-exit policy for release cycles, codified from v1.14 (2026-05-05).

RULE: soak runs to a HARD cap of 14 days. Evaluate at day 7 via reverie_stats period:7d detailed:true; re-check at day 10 and 14 — whichever fires first wins.

CLOCK PEG (codified 2026-06-09): the soak clock pegs to the most recent stable release that CHANGED AGENT-FACING BEHAVIOR — not to every tag. Patch/security releases that don't change agent-facing behavior (per project.patchPolicy) do NOT reset it. Worked example: v1.2.0 (2026-06-09) changed agent-facing behavior → clock starts there; the same-day v1.2.1 (security) and v1.2.2 (perf/quality, no feature surface) patches did NOT reset it. So the v1.2.x soak checkpoints from 2026-06-09: day-7 2026-06-16, re-check day-10, hard cap 2026-06-23.

EXIT GATE (single machine, ALL four required): ≥10 distinct MCP sessions, ≥5 namespaces written across, ≥3 distinct projects active, ≥7 elapsed days. Gate met → exit early, run theme-pick (v1.14 playbook Phase 2). 14d reached with thin signal → ship the smallest scoped theme + carry candidates forward; do NOT extend — longer soaks overfit whichever signal happened to surface and batch more fixes than one release can digest.

CALIBRATION (N=1): anchored on v1.14's soak (exited day 12; single-host 7d snapshot at exit: 16 sessions, 281 calls, 7 namespaces, 4 projects). Gate is deliberately single-machine — cross-machine telemetry isn't aggregable from one host today (v1.15+ candidate: reverie_stats --import / merge tool). Refine with v1.15 data: was the gate too loose or too tight?
